Notes

Everything around you is matter: your desk, the air, water and even you. All matter is made of tiny particles called atoms. Millions of them could fit on a full stop. Scientists use coloured balls to show atoms: each colour is a different type of atom.

STEP 2 · EXPLORE

Elements

8 – 20 min · Task 2 · Criterion A
  • An element is a substance made of only ONE type of atom. It cannot be broken down into simpler substances by chemical reactions.
  • There are 118 known elements, listed in the Periodic Table.
  • Each element has a chemical symbol: one capital letter, or a capital letter followed by a small letter. Examples: oxygen O, hydrogen H, carbon C, iron Fe, copper Cu, gold Au, sodium Na.
  • Some elements exist as single atoms (helium, He). Others exist as molecules of the same atom (oxygen, O₂).

Notes

Build models with modelling clay and toothpicks: hydrogen = white, oxygen = red, carbon = black. A molecule of an ELEMENT has only one colour. A molecule of a COMPOUND has two or more colours. Safety: point toothpicks away from people, do not eat the clay, and wash your hands afterwards.

STEP 3 · TEST

Practical: build molecules

20 – 35 min · Task 3 · Criterion C
  • 1. Roll small balls: 4 white (hydrogen), 4 red (oxygen), 1 black (carbon).
  • 2. Build H₂: join 2 white balls.
  • 3. Build O₂: join 2 red balls.
  • 4. Build H₂O: join 2 white balls to 1 red ball.
  • 5. Build CO₂: join 2 red balls to 1 black ball.
  • 6. For each model, count the atoms and the types of atom.

3.1 (type). Element or compound? [4]
Hydrogen, H₂
Oxygen, O₂

This step: 9 marks
STEP 4 · EXPLAIN

Compounds

35 – 48 min · Task 4 · Criterion A
  • A compound is made of two or more DIFFERENT elements chemically joined together.
  • A compound has a chemical formula. H₂O means 2 hydrogen atoms and 1 oxygen atom. The small number tells you how many atoms; no number means 1.
  • A compound is very different from the elements it is made from: sodium is a soft metal that reacts strongly with water, chlorine is a poisonous green gas, but together they make sodium chloride (NaCl), table salt.
  • A compound can only be split back into its elements by a chemical reaction.
▶ Types of matter: elements, compounds and mixtures (Professor Dave Explains, 4:15)A clear summary with particle diagrams
Teacher demonstration. Burn a short piece of magnesium ribbon. Shiny grey magnesium (an element) joins with oxygen (an element) from the air to make a white powder, magnesium oxide (a compound). Do not look straight at the bright flame.

Notes

Remember: one type of atom = element; two or more different atoms joined = compound.
